I can confirm the behavior by the OP and also can confirm the below workaround as I'm currently using it in my game to get around this issue. 
Work around currently to correct this until resolved.

```
func optimize_android_display():
	if not (OS.has_feature("mobile") or OS.has_feature("android")):
		return
		
	print("Applying Android display optimization trick...")
	
	# Get the current stored resolution preference
	var desired_mode = DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN
	
	if current_resolution_index != 0:  # If not set to native/fullscreen
		desired_mode = DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_MAXIMIZED
	
	# First switch to windowed mode to trigger proper initialization
	print("Step 1: Temporarily switching to windowed mode for optimization")
	DisplayServer.window_set_mode(DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_MAXIMIZED)
	
	# Wait a short time to let rendering stabilize
	await get_tree().create_timer(0.2).timeout
	
	# Then switch to the desired mode if it's fullscreen
	if desired_mode == DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN:
		print("Step 2: Switching back to fullscreen mode with optimized state")
		DisplayServer.window_set_mode(DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN)
		current_resolution_index = 0
```
@felipemdutra, I have confirmed that you need a second screen to monitor this properly. Try connecting a second screen temporarily and open up htop or whatever Arch uses.

> [@uno1982](https://github.com/uno1982), I don't see how that function could affect this issue. Please explain.

it swaps to windowed from native then swaps back ... not sure why this corrects the performance issues with "fullscreen native" but it does.
@uno1982, Is your game a mobile game? That function only affects android to the looks of it.

> Is your game a mobile game? That function only affects android to the looks of it.

yes its a compatabilty renderer mobile title for android/ios but will be ported to steam eventually. I've placed the platform specific checks there due to that ...however like stated the performance impact is there regardless. You just feel it more on mobile... but I can confirm that this swap works to correct the cpu slowdown.
@uno1982, Have you tried this function on desktop?
@uno1982 I mean, I can live with regular fullscreen mode, but some people can't.

> [@uno1982](https://github.com/uno1982) I mean, I can live with regular fullscreen mode, but some people can't.

you don't have to keep it that way. The pure act of swapping then swapping back to exclusive fullscreen mode corrects the issue. Afterwards you don't get the cpu slowdown.... even when changing to windowed etc..... or at least thats the behavior I'm seeing on android currently. Loading the app up in exclusive fullscreen appears to be the issue. Not the setting itself. Loading the app up in windowed then swapping to native doesn't present with the slowdown which is why I applied the above function as a workaround.
@uno1982, where does `current_resolution_index` come from?

> [@uno1982](https://github.com/uno1982), where does `current_resolution_index` come from?

its my array returned from get supported resolutions function. Its just a list of resolutions.
Is that a `DisplayServer` function?

its just a simple index apply and var for storing in the config for load basically 

```
		if index == 0:  # Native Resolution (Full screen)
			DisplayServer.window_set_mode(DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN)
			print("GameManager: Set to FULLSCREEN mode")
		else:  # Windowed
			DisplayServer.window_set_mode(DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_MAXIMIZED)
			print("GameManager: Set to MAXIMIZED mode")
		return
```

```
if config.load("user://settings.cfg") == OK:
		if config.has_section_key("video", "resolution_index"):
			var index = config.get_value("video", "resolution_index", 0)
			current_resolution_index = index
			apply_resolution(index)
```

In my game manager if its not native then I allow for window size settings that are supported by the panel via getting the panel size and using some math to get each smaller aspect ratio resolution.... All of this is a bit outside of the scope for the issue at hand here and I don't want to muddy the water of the focus..... the point here is that the issue appears to be loading the app with fullscreen exclusive and the workaround above appears to handle whatever race condition or init that isn't happening properly to cause the extra cpu load.
